description.description_long: In June 2020, Attorney General William Barr announced that Geoffrey Berman, the U.S. attorney for the Southern District of New York, would be stepping down and that SEC Chairman Jay Clayton would be nominated to replace him. Berman responded publicly that he had not resigned and intended to remain in the position until a Senate-confirmed successor was in place. The next day, Barr said President Donald Trump had fired Berman after Berman refused to resign; Berman then agreed to leave. The Associated Press documented the conflicting announcements and reported Trump’s statement that he was not involved and that Barr was working on the matter. This sequence supports a factual account of the public standoff and Berman’s departure. The original Time link was unavailable and the other supplied link was a general AP topic hub, so they do not support detailed claims about investigations or their outcomes.
